offNote: This process is not clustered: cluster.mode resolved to off. That is correct for one container and WRONG for several against one store.
nodeWorker: {id} ({name}), a request worker of that node
heartbeat: every {every}ms, lifetime {ttl}ms by the database clock
heartbeatFailures: . {n} consecutive failure(s): {error}. A node that cannot renew within its lifetime exits.
barrier: {requests} request(s) waited a mean {wait}ms to catch up; {gaveUp} were served before catching up; {held} response(s) were held a mean {hold}ms for their writes to commit
barrierOff: off — only active-active nodes wait for each other’s writes
noListOff: There is no membership to list: cluster.mode resolved to off, so this process is not a node of anything and writes nothing another node could fence.
noListYet: This process has not read the member list yet. The node is clustered ({mode}); the process that answered reads the membership from the store when it starts and then at most once a heartbeat, and this page was answered before the first read came back. Reload it.
asOf: As of {age}s ago, read at most one heartbeat apart by whichever process answered. Every time below is the database’s clock, which a lifetime is measured against: two containers’ clocks differ. Up is the exception: it is the node’s own process uptime, which no other clock can state.
labelGone: Nodes that have left or expired
restarted: restarted {n} time(s), the last life ended {ago}
agreesNo: NO — two nodes with different values answer the same request two ways
noLive: no live member rows — this node’s own row arrives on its first heartbeat
earlierLives: and {n} earlier life/lives under this name
goneSummary: {n} node(s) that have left or expired
goneNote: One row per node name with no running member: a name that is running again is that node restarted, counted on its running row. A node that stopped cleanly released its leases; one that EXPIRED did not, and its leases waited out their lifetime.
leasesNote: A lease is a named role ONE node holds, with a fencing token that goes up every time it changes hands. A released lease is expired and never deleted, so the token never goes back to 1.
otherNote: This service runs as several cells, each its own cluster against its own database; the list above is this cell’s. Each other cell was asked over the inter-cell channel for its members and pools when this page was answered — names and counts only, never an address.
cellNoAnswer: This cell did not answer. {error} Its members may be running; the inter-cell channel could not ask them.
cellNotClustered: Answered in {ms}ms; it is not clustered (cluster.mode {mode}).
cellSummary: Mode {mode}; answered in {ms}ms. Times are that cell’s database clock, relative to when it answered.
cellGoneSummary: {n} node name(s) that have left or expired
poolsError: Its worker pools could not be read: {error}
capsAccepted: Every capability is provided or accepted as missing ({ids}).
capsMissing: {missing} of {total} are missing, so cluster.mode=active-active refuses to start. Each is a way two nodes give different answers, described under the section of issue #46 named beside it.
capsUnknown: cluster.acceptMissingCapabilities names ids this build does not know: {ids}.
thSource: Where this process’s value came from
